exam_set.title: Practice Set 1
exam_set.description: Textbook Practice — Book 1, Chapter 14, Practice Set 1

questions.jp: プロジェクトの特性はどれか。
questions.romaji: Purojekuto no tokusei wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which choice describes the characteristics of a project?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 独自性はあるが、有限性がない。
options.romaji: Dokujisei wa aru ga, yūgensei ga nai.
options.en: It is unique but not temporary.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 独自性はないが、有限性がある。
options.romaji: Dokujisei wa nai ga, yūgensei ga aru.
options.en: It is not unique but is temporary.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 独自性も有限性もある。
options.en: It is both unique and temporary.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 独自性も有限性もない。
options.en: It is neither unique nor temporary.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A project creates something particular and has a definite beginning and end.

Technical breakdown:
Project-management definitions distinguish projects from routine operations by two core traits: uniqueness and temporariness. A project produces a unique product, service, or result, and its finite duration ends when objectives are achieved or the project is terminated.

Japanese keywords to remember:
独自性 = dokujisei = uniqueness
有限性 = yūgensei = temporariness
特性 = tokusei = characteristic

Why the best solution works:
ウ includes both defining traits required for an activity to be a project.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Without a finite duration, the activity resembles continuing operations.
イ:
A temporary activity that creates no unique result does not fully meet the project definition.
エ:
Lacking both traits describes routine ongoing work.

Memory trick:
Project = unique result plus temporary journey.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: プロジェクトに関わるステークホルダの説明のうち、適切なものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Purojekuto ni kakawaru sutēkuhoruda no setsumei no uchi, tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which statement about project stakeholders is appropriate?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 組織の内部に属しており、組織の外部にいることはない。
options.romaji: Soshiki no naibu ni zoku shite ori, soshiki no gaibu ni iru koto wa nai.
options.en: They belong inside the organization and are never outside it.

options.label: イ
options.jp: プロジェクトに直接参加し、間接的な関与にとどまることはない。
options.romaji: Purojekuto ni chokusetsu sanka shi, kansetsuteki na kan'yo ni todomaru koto wa nai.
options.en: They participate directly and are never involved only indirectly.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: プロジェクトの成果が、自らの利益になる者と不利益になる者がいる。
options.romaji: Purojekuto no seika ga, mizukara no rieki ni naru mono to furieki ni naru mono ga iru.
options.en: Some benefit from the project outcome, while others may be disadvantaged by it.

options.label: エ
options.jp: プロジェクトマネージャのように、個人として特定できることが必要である。
options.romaji: Purojekuto manējā no yō ni, kojin to shite tokutei dekiru koto ga hitsuyō de aru.
options.en: They must be identifiable as individuals, like the project manager.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A stakeholder is anyone affected by a project, including people who gain, lose, support, or oppose it.

Technical breakdown:
Stakeholders may be internal or external, directly or indirectly involved, and individuals, groups, or organizations. Their interests can be positive or negative because project outcomes can create benefits, costs, risks, or disruption.

Japanese keywords to remember:
ステークホルダ = sutēkuhoruda = stakeholder
成果 = seika = outcome
利益・不利益 = rieki furieki = benefit and disadvantage

Why the best solution works:
ウ correctly recognizes that affected parties can evaluate the same project outcome differently.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Customers, regulators, suppliers, and communities can be external stakeholders.
イ:
People affected indirectly are also stakeholders.
エ:
A stakeholder can be a group or organization and need not be one named individual.

Memory trick:
Stakeholder = anyone who affects or is affected.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: ソフトウェア開発プロジェクトにおいてWBS（Work Breakdown Structure）を使用する目的として、適切なものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Sofutowea kaihatsu purojekuto ni oite WBS (Work Breakdown Structure) o shiyō suru mokuteki to shite, tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: What is an appropriate purpose of using a WBS in a software-development project?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 開発の期間と費用がトレードオフの関係にある場合に、総費用の最適化を図る。
options.romaji: Kaihatsu no kikan to hiyō ga torēdo ofu no kankei ni aru baai ni, sōhiyō no saitekika o hakaru.
options.en: Optimize total cost when development duration and cost have a trade-off relationship.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 作業の順序関係を明確にして、重点管理すべきクリティカルパスを把握する。
options.romaji: Sagyō no junjo kankei o meikaku ni shite, jūten kanri subeki kuritikaru pasu o haaku suru.
options.en: Clarify task order and identify the critical path requiring focused management.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 作業の日程を横棒（バー）で表して、作業の開始時点や終了時点、現時点の進捗を明確にする。
options.romaji: Sagyō no nittei o yokobō (bā) de arawashite, sagyō no kaishi jiten ya shūryō jiten, genjiten no shinchoku o meikaku ni suru.
options.en: Use horizontal bars to show task schedules, start and end points, and current progress.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 作業を階層的に詳細化して、管理可能な大きさに細分化する。
options.romaji: Sagyō o kaisōteki ni shōsaika shite, kanri kanō na ōkisa ni saibunka suru.
options.en: Refine work hierarchically and divide it into manageable units.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A WBS breaks one large project into smaller pieces that people can estimate, assign, and manage.

Technical breakdown:
A Work Breakdown Structure decomposes project deliverables and work hierarchically until work packages are manageable. It defines scope and supports estimation and responsibility assignment; it does not itself show sequence, calendar bars, or cost-time optimization.

Japanese keywords to remember:
階層的 = kaisōteki = hierarchical
細分化する = saibunka suru = subdivide
管理可能 = kanri kanō = manageable

Why the best solution works:
エ states the defining WBS operation: hierarchical decomposition into manageable work packages.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Cost-duration optimization is a time-cost analysis task.
イ:
Critical-path identification uses a network schedule such as PERT or CPM.
ウ:
Horizontal schedule bars describe a Gantt chart.

Memory trick:
WBS: break work smaller.

Correct answer: エ

questions.jp: システムを構成するプログラムの本数とプログラム1本当たりのコーディング所要工数が表のとおりであるとき、システムを95日間で開発するには少なくとも何人の要員が必要か。ここで、システムの開発にはコーディングのほかに、設計及びテストの作業が必要であり、それらの作業にはコーディング所要工数の8倍の工数が掛かるものとする。表：入力処理は20本で1本当たり1人日、出力処理は10本で1本当たり3人日、計算処理は5本で1本当たり9人日。
questions.romaji: Shisutemu o kōsei suru puroguramu no honsū to puroguramu ippon atari no kōdingu shoyō kōsū ga hyō no tōri de aru toki, shisutemu o kyūjūgo nichikan de kaihatsu suru ni wa sukunakutomo nannin no yōin ga hitsuyō ka. Koko de, shisutemu no kaihatsu ni wa kōdingu no hoka ni, sekkei oyobi tesuto no sagyō ga hitsuyō de ari, sorera no sagyō ni wa kōdingu shoyō kōsū no hachibai no kōsū ga kakaru mono to suru. Hyō: nyūryoku shori wa nijuppon de ippon atari ichi ninnichi, shutsuryoku shori wa juppon de ippon atari san ninnichi, keisan shori wa gohon de ippon atari kyū ninnichi.
questions.en: Given the program counts and coding effort per program, what minimum staff is needed to develop the system in 95 days? Design and testing require eight times the coding effort. Input: 20 programs × 1 person-day; output: 10 × 3; calculation: 5 × 9.
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Add all coding days, add eight times that amount for design and testing, then divide by 95 days.

Technical breakdown:
Coding effort = 20×1 + 10×3 + 5×9 = 20 + 30 + 45 = 95 person-days. Design and testing = 8×95 = 760 person-days. Total = 95 + 760 = 855 person-days. Required staff = 855÷95 = 9 people.

Japanese keywords to remember:
所要工数 = shoyō kōsū = required effort
人日 = ninnichi = person-day
少なくとも = sukunakutomo = at least

Why the best solution works:
イ is the exact quotient of total required effort divided by the fixed 95-day duration.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Eight is the multiplier for non-coding work, not the required staff count.
ウ:
Twelve exceeds the calculated minimum of nine.
エ:
Thirteen also exceeds the calculated minimum.

Memory trick:
People = total person-days ÷ available days.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: 開発期間10か月、開発工数200人月のプロジェクトを計画する。次の配分表を前提とすると、ピーク時の要員は何人か。ここで、各工程では開始から終了までの要員数は一定とする。工数配分は、要件定義16％、設計33％、開発・テスト42％、システムテスト9％。期間配分は、要件定義20％、設計30％、開発・テスト40％、システムテスト10％。
questions.romaji: Kaihatsu kikan jikkagetsu, kaihatsu kōsū nihyaku ningetsu no purojekuto o keikaku suru. Tsugi no haibunhyō o zentei to suru to, pīkuji no yōin wa nannin ka. Koko de, kaku kōtei de wa kaishi kara shūryō made no yōinsū wa ittei to suru. Kōsū haibun wa, yōken teigi jūroku pāsento, sekkei sanjūsan pāsento, kaihatsu tesuto yonjūni pāsento, shisutemu tesuto kyū pāsento. Kikan haibun wa, yōken teigi nijū pāsento, sekkei sanjū pāsento, kaihatsu tesuto yonjū pāsento, shisutemu tesuto jū pāsento.
questions.en: Plan a 10-month, 200-person-month project. Effort allocation: requirements 16%, design 33%, development/testing 42%, system testing 9%. Duration allocation: 20%, 30%, 40%, 10%. Staffing is constant within each phase. What is peak staffing?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
For each phase, divide its share of work by its share of time. The largest result is the peak team.

Technical breakdown:
Requirements: 200×0.16=32 person-months; 10×0.20=2 months; 32÷2=16 people. Design: 66÷3=22. Development/testing: 84÷4=21. System testing: 18÷1=18. The maximum is 22 people during design.

Japanese keywords to remember:
工数配分 = kōsū haibun = effort allocation
期間配分 = kikan haibun = duration allocation
ピーク時 = pīkuji = peak time

Why the best solution works:
エ matches the largest phase staffing calculation, 22.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Eighteen is system-test staffing.
イ:
Twenty is not produced by any phase calculation.
ウ:
Twenty-one is development/testing staffing, below the design peak.

Memory trick:
Phase staff = phase effort ÷ phase months; choose maximum.

Correct answer: エ

questions.jp: システム開発の進捗管理などに用いられるトレンドチャートの説明はどれか。
questions.romaji: Shisutemu kaihatsu no shinchoku kanri nado ni mochiirareru torendo chāto no setsumei wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which statement describes a trend chart used for system-development progress management?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 作業に関与する人と責任をマトリックス状に示したもの
options.romaji: Sagyō ni kan'yo suru hito to sekinin o matorikkusu-jō ni shimeshita mono
options.en: A matrix showing people involved in work and their responsibilities.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 作業日程の計画と実績を対比できるように帯状に示したもの
options.romaji: Sagyō nittei no keikaku to jisseki o taihi dekiru yō ni obi-jō ni shimeshita mono
options.en: A bar display comparing planned and actual work schedules.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 作業の進捗状況と、予算の消費状況を関連付けて折れ線で示したもの
options.romaji: Sagyō no shinchoku jōkyō to, yosan no shōhi jōkyō o kanren-zukete oresen de shimeshita mono
options.en: A line chart relating work progress to budget consumption.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 作業の順序や相互関係をネットワーク状に示したもの
options.romaji: Sagyō no junjo ya sōgo kankei o nettowāku-jō ni shimeshita mono
options.en: A network showing task sequence and interrelationships.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A trend chart draws lines over time so you can compare how much work is complete with how much budget has been spent.

Technical breakdown:
Trend charts visualize time-series movement in progress and cost, making deviations and worsening tendencies visible. The other choices describe a responsibility matrix, Gantt chart, and network diagram.

Japanese keywords to remember:
進捗状況 = shinchoku jōkyō = progress status
予算の消費状況 = yosan no shōhi jōkyō = budget consumption
折れ線 = oresen = line graph

Why the best solution works:
ウ captures both tracked dimensions and the line-based trend presentation.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
People and responsibilities in a matrix describe a responsibility assignment matrix.
イ:
Planned and actual schedules shown as bars describe a Gantt chart.
エ:
Task sequence and relationships shown as a network describe PERT or CPM.

Memory trick:
Trend chart = progress line plus spending line over time.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: 二つのアクティビティが次の関係にあるとき、論理的な依存関係はどれか。“システム要件定義プロセス”が完了すれば、“システム方式設計プロセス”が開始できる。
questions.romaji: Futatsu no akutibiti ga tsugi no kankei ni aru toki, ronriteki na izon kankei wa dore ka. 'Shisutemu yōken teigi purosesu' ga kanryō sureba, 'shisutemu hōshiki sekkei purosesu' ga kaishi dekiru.
questions.en: When system architectural design can start after system requirements definition finishes, what is the logical dependency?

options.label: ア
options.jp: FF関係（Finish-to-Finish）
options.en: Finish-to-Finish

options.label: イ
options.jp: FS関係（Finish-to-Start）
options.en: Finish-to-Start

options.label: ウ
options.jp: SF関係（Start-to-Finish）
options.en: Start-to-Finish

options.label: エ
options.jp: SS関係（Start-to-Start）
options.en: Start-to-Start

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
The first task must finish before the next task may start.

Technical breakdown:
A Finish-to-Start dependency means successor start depends on predecessor finish. Here requirements definition is the predecessor and architectural design is the successor, matching the stated completion-to-start condition exactly.

Japanese keywords to remember:
完了 = kanryō = finish
開始 = kaishi = start
依存関係 = izon kankei = dependency

Why the best solution works:
イ maps the wording directly: Finish of requirements → Start of design.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
FF links the finish times of both activities.
ウ:
SF makes successor finish depend on predecessor start.
エ:
SS links the start times of both activities.

Memory trick:
Finish then Start = FS.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: アローダイアグラムで表されるプロジェクトは、完了までに最少で何日を要するか。作業はA＝30日の後、B＝5日、C＝30日、D＝20日に分岐する。B完了点からC完了点へ、C完了点からD完了点へダミー作業がある。合流点へはB後のE＝40日、C後のF＝25日、D後のG＝30日が入り、その後H＝30日を行う。
questions.romaji: Arō daiyaguramu de arawasareru purojekuto wa, kanryō made ni saisū de nannichi o yō suru ka. Sagyō wa A ikōru sanjūnichi no ato, B ikōru gonichi, C ikōru sanjūnichi, D ikōru nijūnichi ni bunki suru. B kanryōten kara C kanryōten e, C kanryōten kara D kanryōten e damī sagyō ga aru. Gōryūten e wa B-go no E ikōru yonjūnichi, C-go no F ikōru nijūgonichi, D-go no G ikōru sanjūnichi ga hairi, sono ato H ikōru sanjūnichi o okonau.
questions.en: What is the minimum project duration? After A=30 days, branches B=5, C=30, D=20 begin. Dummy activities constrain B completion before C's node and C completion before D's node. E=40 follows B, F=25 follows C, G=30 follows D; they merge before H=30.
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A merge must wait for every required incoming route. Dummy arrows can make a later branch wait even though they add zero days.

Technical breakdown:
After A, earliest times are B end=35, C end=max(30+30,35)=60 because of the B→C dummy, and D end=max(30+20,60)=60 because of the C→D dummy. Ends at the merge are E:35+40=75, F:60+25=85, G:60+30=90. The merge waits until day 90; H adds 30, giving 120 days.

Japanese keywords to remember:
アローダイアグラム = arō daiyaguramu = arrow diagram
ダミー作業 = damī sagyō = dummy activity
最少 = saisū = minimum

Why the best solution works:
ウ includes the dependency delays carried by both zero-duration dummy arrows.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
105 ignores part of the dependency-constrained longest route.
イ:
115 still understates the earliest merge time.
エ:
125 adds five days not present on the critical route.

Memory trick:
At every merge, take maximum arrival time.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: あるプロジェクトの日程計画をアローダイアグラムで示す。クリティカルパスはどれか。開始点から上側へA＝1日、下側へB＝5日。Aの後はD＝3日で上側合流点へ、又はC＝3日で下側点へ進む。Bも下側点へ入り、そこからE＝4日で下側合流点へ進む。下側合流点から上側合流点へダミー作業がある。終点へは上側合流点からG＝4日、下側合流点からF＝5日。
questions.romaji: Aru purojekuto no nittei keikaku o arō daiyaguramu de shimesu. Kuritikaru pasu wa dore ka. Kaishiten kara uwagawa e A ikōru ichinichi, shitagawa e B ikōru gonichi. A no ato wa D ikōru sannichi de uwagawa gōryūten e, mata wa C ikōru sannichi de shitagawaten e susumu. B mo shitagawaten e hairi, soko kara E ikōru yokka de shitagawa gōryūten e susumu. Shitagawa gōryūten kara uwagawa gōryūten e damī sagyō ga aru. Shūten e wa uwagawa gōryūten kara G ikōru yokka, shitagawa gōryūten kara F ikōru gonichi.
questions.en: Which is the critical path? Start branches to A=1 and B=5. A leads through D=3 to the upper merge or C=3 to the lower node. B also enters the lower node, followed by E=4 to the lower merge. A dummy leads from lower to upper merge. Finish is reached by G=4 from upper or F=5 from lower.

options.label: ア
options.jp: A、C、E、F
options.en: A, C, E, F

options.label: イ
options.jp: A、D、G
options.en: A, D, G

options.label: ウ
options.jp: B、E、F
options.en: B, E, F

options.label: エ
options.jp: B、E、G
options.en: B, E, G

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
The critical path is the longest dependent route; any delay on it delays the project.

Technical breakdown:
A,C reaches the lower node in 1+3=4 days, while B reaches it in 5, so B controls. After E, the lower merge is at 5+4=9. From there F gives 9+5=14. The dummy also delays the upper merge to day 9, then G gives 13. A,D,G is only 1+3+4=8. Therefore B,E,F is longest at 14 days.

Japanese keywords to remember:
クリティカルパス = kuritikaru pasu = critical path
日程計画 = nittei keikaku = schedule plan
作業日数 = sagyō nissū = activity duration

Why the best solution works:
ウ follows the controlling arrivals and totals the maximum project duration.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
A,C does not control the shared node because B arrives later.
イ:
A,D,G totals only eight days.
エ:
B,E controls the upper merge, but G finishes in thirteen days, shorter than F's fourteen.

Memory trick:
Critical path = longest valid dependency route.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: プロジェクトのスケジュールを短縮するために、アクティビティに割り当てる資源を増やして、アクティビティの所要期間を短縮する技法はどれか。
questions.romaji: Purojekuto no sukejūru o tanshuku suru tame ni, akutibiti ni wariateru shigen o fuyashite, akutibiti no shoyō kikan o tanshuku suru gihō wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which technique shortens a project schedule by increasing resources assigned to activities and reducing their duration?

options.label: ア
options.jp: クラッシング
options.en: Crashing

options.label: イ
options.jp: クリティカルチェーン法
options.en: Critical chain method

options.label: ウ
options.jp: ファストトラッキング
options.en: Fast tracking

options.label: エ
options.jp: モンテカルロ法
options.en: Monte Carlo method

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Crashing spends more resources to finish important work sooner.

Technical breakdown:
Crashing compresses schedule duration by adding staff, equipment, overtime, or other resources, normally to critical-path activities. It often increases direct cost and may introduce coordination risk, so cost per unit of time saved is evaluated.

Japanese keywords to remember:
資源を増やす = shigen o fuyasu = increase resources
所要期間 = shoyō kikan = required duration
クラッシング = kurasshingu = crashing

Why the best solution works:
ア directly matches resource addition to activity-duration reduction.

Wrong answer analysis:
イ:
Critical chain manages resource constraints and buffers.
ウ:
Fast tracking overlaps activities that were planned sequentially.
エ:
Monte Carlo simulation analyzes uncertainty and schedule probability.

Memory trick:
Crash = add resources; fast-track = overlap work.

Correct answer: ア

questions.jp: ファストトラッキング技法を用いてスケジュールの短縮を行う。当初の計画は図1のとおりである。作業Eを作業E1、E2、E3に分けて、図2のように計画を変更すると、スケジュールは全体で何日短縮できるか。図1：A＝5、B＝8、C＝7、D＝7、E＝9、F＝5、G＝7、H＝4、I＝2。図2：EをE1＝3、E2＝4、E3＝2に分け、E1とE2を並行し、両方の完了後にE3を行う。
questions.romaji: Fasuto torakkingu gihō o mochiite sukejūru no tanshuku o okonau. Tōsho no keikaku wa zu ichi no tōri de aru. Sagyō E o sagyō E1, E2, E3 ni wakete, zu ni no yō ni keikaku o henkō suru to, sukejūru wa zentai de nannichi tanshuku dekiru ka. Zu ichi: A ikōru go, B ikōru hachi, C ikōru nana, D ikōru nana, E ikōru kyū, F ikōru go, G ikōru nana, H ikōru yon, I ikōru ni. Zu ni: E o E1 ikōru san, E2 ikōru yon, E3 ikōru ni ni wake, E1 to E2 o heikō shi, ryōhō no kanryōgo ni E3 o okonau.
questions.en: Using fast tracking, how many days is the whole schedule shortened? Original durations: A=5, B=8, C=7, D=7, E=9, F=5, G=7, H=4, I=2. E is split into parallel E1=3 and E2=4, followed after both by E3=2.
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Parallelizing E makes that route faster, but another route then becomes the longest, limiting total project savings.

Technical breakdown:
Originally the longest route is A+B+E+H+I = 5+8+9+4+2 = 28 days. The competing A+B+D+G route is 5+8+7+7 = 27 days. Modified E duration is max(E1 3,E2 4)+E3 2 = 6, so its route becomes 25 days. The unchanged 27-day route becomes critical. Total shortening = 28−27 = 1 day.

Japanese keywords to remember:
ファストトラッキング = fasuto torakkingu = fast tracking
並行 = heikō = parallel
短縮 = tanshuku = shortening

Why the best solution works:
ア accounts for the critical path shifting to the unchanged 27-day route.

Wrong answer analysis:
イ:
Two days does not equal the difference between the original and new project critical durations.
ウ:
Three is E's own reduction, but project reduction is capped by another path.
エ:
Four overstates both E's effective reduction and total schedule saving.

Memory trick:
After shortening one path, recalculate all paths.

Correct answer: ア

questions.jp: ファンクションポイント法の説明はどれか。
questions.romaji: Fankushon pointo-hō no setsumei wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which statement describes the function point method?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 開発するプログラムごとのステップ数を積算し、開発規模を見積もる。
options.romaji: Kaihatsu suru puroguramu goto no suteppu-sū o sekisan shi, kaihatsu kibo o mitsumoru.
options.en: Sum program steps to estimate development size.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 開発プロジェクトで必要な作業のWBSを作成し、各作業の工数を見積もる。
options.romaji: Kaihatsu purojekuto de hitsuyō na sagyō no WBS o sakusei shi, kaku sagyō no kōsū o mitsumoru.
options.en: Create a WBS and estimate each task's effort.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 外部入出力や内部論理ファイル、照会、インタフェースなどの個数や特性などから開発規模を見積もる。
options.romaji: Gaibu nyūshutsuryoku ya naibu ronri fairu, shōkai, intafēsu nado no kosū ya tokusei nado kara kaihatsu kibo o mitsumoru.
options.en: Estimate size from counts and characteristics of external inputs/outputs, internal logical files, inquiries, and interfaces.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 過去の類似例を探し、その実績との差異などを分析評価して開発規模を見積もる。
options.romaji: Kako no ruiji-rei o sagashi, sono jisseki to no sai nado o bunseki hyōka shite kaihatsu kibo o mitsumoru.
options.en: Find a similar past case and estimate size by analyzing differences from its actual results.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Function points measure how much useful functionality users receive, instead of counting code lines.

Technical breakdown:
The method counts user-visible functional types such as external inputs, outputs, inquiries, internal logical files, and external interface files, weights them by complexity, and applies adjustment when required. It is technology-independent compared with source-line counts.

Japanese keywords to remember:
ファンクションポイント法 = fankushon pointo-hō = function point method
外部入出力 = gaibu nyūshutsuryoku = external input/output
開発規模 = kaihatsu kibo = development size

Why the best solution works:
ウ lists the functional elements used by the method.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Counting program steps is source lines-of-code estimation.
イ:
Estimating WBS tasks is bottom-up effort estimation.
エ:
Using a similar past case is analogy estimation.

Memory trick:
Function points count user functions, not code.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: リスクが顕在化しても、その影響が小さいと想定されるので、損害の負担を受容するリスク対応はどれか。
questions.romaji: Risuku ga kenzaika shite mo, sono eikyō ga chiisai to sōtei sareru node, songai no futan o juyō suru risuku taiō wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which risk response accepts the loss because the impact is expected to be small even if the risk occurs?

options.label: ア
options.jp: リスク移転
options.en: Risk transfer

options.label: イ
options.jp: リスク回避
options.en: Risk avoidance

options.label: ウ
options.jp: リスク低減
options.en: Risk mitigation

options.label: エ
options.jp: リスク保有
options.en: Risk retention

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
If a possible loss is small, the project may knowingly keep the risk and pay if it happens.

Technical breakdown:
Risk retention, also called acceptance, means taking no action to eliminate or transfer the threat beyond monitoring or preparing a contingency. It is rational when treatment cost exceeds expected loss or impact is tolerable.

Japanese keywords to remember:
リスク保有 = risuku hoyū = risk retention
顕在化 = kenzaika = materialization
受容する = juyō suru = accept

Why the best solution works:
エ directly describes keeping responsibility for the loss.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Transfer shifts financial consequences to another party, such as an insurer.
イ:
Avoidance removes the risky activity or cause.
ウ:
Mitigation reduces probability or impact through controls.

Memory trick:
Small tolerable risk: retain it.

Correct answer: エ

questions.jp: あるソフトウェアにおいて、機能の個数と機能の複雑度に対する重み付け係数は表のとおりである。このソフトウェアのファンクションポイント値は幾らか。ここで、ソフトウェアの全体的な複雑さの補正係数は0.75とする。表：外部入力は個数1、重み付け係数4。外部出力は個数2、重み付け係数5。内部論理ファイルは個数1、重み付け係数10。
questions.romaji: Aru sofutowea ni oite, kinō no kosū to kinō no fukuzatsudo ni taisuru omomizuke keisū wa hyō no tōri de aru. Kono sofutowea no fankushon pointo-chi wa ikura ka. Koko de, sofutowea no zentaiteki na fukuzatsusa no hosei keisū wa rei ten nanago to suru. Hyō: gaibu nyūryoku wa kosū ichi, omomizuke keisū yon. Gaibu shutsuryoku wa kosū ni, omomizuke keisū go. Naibu ronri fairu wa kosū ichi, omomizuke keisū jū.
questions.en: Calculate the function point value. External inputs: 1×4; external outputs: 2×5; internal logical files: 1×10. Overall complexity adjustment coefficient is 0.75.
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Multiply each function count by its weight, add the results, then apply the adjustment.

Technical breakdown:
Unadjusted function points = 1×4 + 2×5 + 1×10 = 4+10+10 = 24. Apply overall complexity coefficient: 24×0.75 = 18. Therefore the adjusted function point value is 18.

Japanese keywords to remember:
重み付け係数 = omomizuke keisū = weighting coefficient
補正係数 = hosei keisū = adjustment coefficient
内部論理ファイル = naibu ronri fairu = internal logical file

Why the best solution works:
ア follows both required calculation stages and preserves the 0.75 adjustment.

Wrong answer analysis:
イ:
Twenty-four is the unadjusted subtotal before multiplying by 0.75.
ウ:
Thirty is not produced by the supplied counts, weights, and coefficient.
エ:
Thirty-two would incorrectly reverse the adjustment by dividing 24 by 0.75.

Memory trick:
FP = weighted function sum × adjustment.

Correct answer: ア

questions.jp: プロジェクトの日程計画を作成するのに適した技法はどれか。
questions.romaji: Purojekuto no nittei keikaku o sakusei suru no ni tekishita gihō wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which technique is suitable for creating a project schedule?

options.label: ア
options.jp: PERT
options.en: PERT

options.label: イ
options.jp: 回帰分析
options.en: Regression analysis

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 時系列分析
options.en: Time-series analysis

options.label: エ
options.jp: 線形計画法
options.en: Linear programming

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
PERT connects tasks in dependency order and calculates when the project can finish.

Technical breakdown:
PERT is a network scheduling technique that models activity dependencies and durations, calculates earliest and latest times, and identifies the critical path. This directly supports project schedule creation and control.

Japanese keywords to remember:
日程計画 = nittei keikaku = schedule planning
PERT = PERT = Program Evaluation and Review Technique
技法 = gihō = technique

Why the best solution works:
ア is designed specifically for dependency-based project scheduling.

Wrong answer analysis:
イ:
Regression analysis estimates relationships among variables.
ウ:
Time-series analysis studies values observed over time for trends or forecasts.
エ:
Linear programming optimizes an objective under constraints.

Memory trick:
PERT draws the path to project completion.

Correct answer: ア

questions.jp: プロジェクト全体のスケジュールを短縮する技法の一つである“クラッシング”では、メンバーの時間外勤務を増やしたり、業務内容に精通したメンバーを新たに増員したりする。“クラッシング”を行う際に、優先的に資源を投入すべきスケジュールアクティビティはどれか。
questions.romaji: Purojekuto zentai no sukejūru o tanshuku suru gihō no hitotsu de aru 'kurasshingu' de wa, menbā no jikangai kinmu o fuyashitari, gyōmu naiyō ni seitsū shita menbā o arata ni zōin shitari suru. 'Kurasshingu' o okonau sai ni, yūsenteki ni shigen o tōnyū subeki sukejūru akutibiti wa dore ka.
questions.en: Crashing shortens a project by adding overtime or skilled members. Which schedule activity should receive resources first?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 業務の難易度が最も高いスケジュールアクティビティ
options.romaji: Gyōmu no nan'ido ga mottomo takai sukejūru akutibiti
options.en: The schedule activity with the highest difficulty.

options.label: イ
options.jp: クリティカルパス上のスケジュールアクティビティ
options.en: A schedule activity on the critical path.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 資源が確保できる時期に開始するスケジュールアクティビティ
options.romaji: Shigen ga kakuho dekiru jiki ni kaishi suru sukejūru akutibiti
options.en: An activity starting when resources become available.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 所要期間を最も長く必要とするスケジュールアクティビティ
options.romaji: Shoyō kikan o mottomo nagaku hitsuyō to suru sukejūru akutibiti
options.en: The single activity requiring the longest duration.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Only shortening work that controls the finish date can immediately shorten the whole project.

Technical breakdown:
Critical-path activities have zero or minimal total float. Reducing a noncritical activity while it still has float does not change project completion. Crashing therefore prioritizes critical activities, usually selecting those with feasible compression and lowest added cost per time unit.

Japanese keywords to remember:
時間外勤務 = jikangai kinmu = overtime
資源を投入する = shigen o tōnyū suru = allocate resources
クリティカルパス上 = kuritikaru pasu-jō = on the critical path

Why the best solution works:
イ targets activities whose duration currently determines the project finish date.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Difficulty alone does not show that shortening the activity affects completion.
ウ:
Resource availability timing does not identify schedule control.
エ:
The longest individual activity may be noncritical and have float.

Memory trick:
To shorten project, shorten critical path.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: プロジェクトのリスクに対応する戦略として、損害発生時のリスクに備え、損害賠償保険に加入することにした。PMBOKによれば、該当する戦略はどれか。
questions.romaji: Purojekuto no risuku ni taiō suru senryaku to shite, songai hasseiji no risuku ni sonae, songai baishō hoken ni kanyū suru koto ni shita. PMBOK ni yoreba, gaitō suru senryaku wa dore ka.
questions.en: A project buys liability insurance to prepare for losses if a risk occurs. According to PMBOK, which strategy is this?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 回避
options.en: Avoidance

options.label: イ
options.jp: 軽減
options.en: Mitigation

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 受容
options.en: Acceptance

options.label: エ
options.jp: 転嫁
options.en: Transfer

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Insurance moves the financial burden of a loss to an insurer in exchange for a premium.

Technical breakdown:
Risk transfer assigns ownership of some financial impact to a third party through insurance, warranties, guarantees, or contracts. The underlying event may still occur, but the agreed financial consequence is shifted.

Japanese keywords to remember:
損害賠償保険 = songai baishō hoken = liability insurance
加入する = kanyū suru = enroll or purchase
転嫁 = tenka = transfer

Why the best solution works:
エ describes shifting the loss burden to the insurance company by contract.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Avoidance eliminates the threat by changing scope or approach.
イ:
Mitigation reduces probability or impact through preventive action.
ウ:
Acceptance keeps the risk and its consequences rather than transferring them.

Memory trick:
Insurance = risk transfer.

Correct answer: エ
